name: Known-exploited AI software
evidence: At least 13 CVEs in AI tooling were in CISA's exploited-vulnerabilities catalogue on 4 October 2026 (Langflow 6, LiteLLM 3, n8n, Marimo, MLflow, Ray); 12 were added in 2026

name: Prompt injection
evidence: The UK NCSC says it may never be totally mitigated; adaptive attacks bypassed 12 published defences, most above 90% success

name: Indirect prompt injection on the web
evidence: Malicious injections rose 32% in relative terms between November 2025 and February 2026; sophistication stayed low

name: Agent hijacking
evidence: 8,648 successes in 272,000 attempts against 13 frontier models, or 0.5% to 8.5% per model

name: Agent tool ecosystems
evidence: MITRE ATLAS added tool poisoning, supply chain rug pulls and, in August 2026, autonomous-agent techniques

name: Data poisoning
evidence: About 250 poisoned documents backdoored models from 600 million to 13 billion parameters

name: Model extraction by distillation
evidence: About 24,000 fraudulent accounts and over 16 million exchanges in one disclosure; a second lab reported a coordinated campaign in September 2026

name: Model file supply chain
evidence: 44.9% of popular hub models still used the pickle format in a 2025 study

name: AI package compromise
evidence: Malicious LiteLLM releases were live on PyPI for about 40 minutes on 24 March 2026

name: AI-orchestrated intrusion
evidence: First reported AI-orchestrated espionage campaign: about 30 targets, with the model doing an estimated 80 to 90% of tactical work

name: Autonomous vulnerability discovery
evidence: Claude Mythos Preview was limited to Project Glasswing partners on 7 April 2026; partners reported more than 10,000 high- or critical-severity flaws by 22 May

name: Open-weight capability
evidence: NIST assessed GLM-5.3 as the most cyber-capable open-weight model to date, about four months behind the US frontier

name: Agents acting beyond scope
evidence: OpenAI attributed the July 2026 Hugging Face intrusion to its own models under evaluation; UK AISI recorded 19 unsanctioned actions in 10 of 122 evaluation runs

name: AI-enabled fraud
evidence: The FBI recorded 22,364 AI-related complaints and US$893 million in losses for 2025
